title: MVDC RBC Stray Dog Collection Service - AWARD
description:
Mole Valley District Council and Runnymede Borough Council invites tenders for the provision of stray dog collection services as set out in these documents. 
      
      The Commencement Date for the delivery of the ​services​ is scheduled to be on 27th May 2025 for Mole Valley District Council and 1st April 2025 for Runnymede Borough Council (both at 00:00 hours).  Each Council will be awarding their own Contract for the provision of all services detailed within their own Specification. 
      
      For Mole Valley District Council, the Contract will be awarded for a time period until 31st March 2028, with an option to extend for a further 2-year period (made up of 2 individual 12 month periods) subject to performance and the absolute discretion of the Council.  Mole Valley District Council has an inter-authority agreement in place with Tandridge District Council. The services provided as part of this contract will service both Tandridge and Mole Valley District Council areas. 
       
      For Runnymede Borough Council, the Contract will be awarded for a period of 3 years until 31st March 2028, with an option to extend for a further 2-year period (made up of 2 individual 12 month periods) subject to performance and the absolute discretion of the Council.   
      
      The tender is split into three lots - Lot 1: Mole Valley and Tandridge District Councils - Lot 2: Runnymede Borough Council - Lot 3: All Councils. Tenderers can bid on lots 1, 2 or 3. The purpose of lot 3 is to investigate if there is any efficiencies for the councils sharing one provider and therefore if you are bidding for this lot, the expectation is that your bid will reflect this.

title: RMBC - PT - Property Advisors 1 - AWARD
description:
Runnymede is a relatively compact borough in the County of Surrey with a population of approximately 80,500 covering an area of 7,804ha. The Council's land and property assets are diverse. Runnymede Borough Council (the Council) owns a commercial investment property portfolio principally comprising office, industrial and retail property investments leased on commercial terms. Along with operational assets across the borough.
      
      1.1.	The delivery of the corporate property strategy covers all aspects of the portfolio to bring best value through improved asset management (investment portfolio), cost management (corporate portfolio) and supporting the organisation in ensuring assets support the wider community objectives of the Council where appropriate.
      
      1.2.	The Council also owns properties which support operational delivery e.g., offices, community centres, pavilions, a depot which are held in support of wider Council initiatives and / or to provide a larger land ownership for longer term redevelopment opportunities or to bring forward other socio-economic benefits.
      
      1.3.	The strategy was developed in-house; however, it is anticipated advice will be required to implement the strategy to maximise the returns of the portfolio as the Council looks to the future of its holding.
      
      1.4.	The services requirement of this specification and the tender process are to be instructed on a call off basis, as and when required by the Council, this contract places no obligation on the Council to instruct or purchase any particular service.
      
      1.5.	The Council invites responses for the provision of this requirement in accordance with the terms & conditions, and the terms as set out in this document.
      
      1.6.	The Council is conducting this further competition from the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 compliant framework Crown Commercial Services (CCS) Framework, RM6168 Estate Management Lot 1: Total Estate Management in order to appoint a Contractor to best meet the requirement.

title: Professional Consultancy Services for the Enterprise M3 Local Enterprise
description:
This is award notice is published on behalf of The Enterprise M3 Local Enterprise Partnership.

Enterprise M3 Local Enterprise Partnership's are appointing a Professional Consultancy Services for the Enterprise M3 Local Enterprise Partnership's multi-site Enterprise Zone, in Hampshire and Surrey & have been supplied with the attached documents.

Enterprise M3 Local Enterprise Partnership (LEP) established a multi-site Enterprise Zone in April 2017 seeking to deliver 10,000 jobs and support 131 businesses. The Zone relates to three sites covering around 40 hectares in Hampshire and Surrey: 

i.	'Basing View' in Basingstoke, Hampshire; 
ii.	'Longcross Park' in Chertsey, Surrey and, 
iii.	Whitehill & Bordon in Hampshire. 

An initial 5-year Implementation Plan was developed and undertaken between 2017- 2022. Over £24 million of investment has delivered new infrastructure and enabled site development at each of the three Zone sites. With the completion of this initial investment period, Enterprise M3 LEP is seeking to commission multi-disciplinary consultancy support that will take the zone to the next stage of delivery and support partners in maximising the jobs, economic growth and business rates retained income over the remaining 20 years of EZ status.

The objective of the commission is to provide information and documentation that will inform and support the development of the second Implementation Plan that reflects the long-term objectives for the three sites, the key partners and the LEP.

This information will provide an evidence base for additional investment required across the multi-site Enterprise Zone. 

Since the information and Implementation Plan will be jointly owned by all parties engaged in this programme (Basingstoke and Deane Borough Council, East Hampshire District Council and Runnymede Borough Council) it will be essential for the Service Provider to engage fully with these parties throughout the contract period.
